correctness.rationale: If two deleted-matching pairs are disjoint from an adjacency resolving set, their two A-side vertices have identical truncated distance vectors, so the set meets n-1 matched pairs. A size n-1 set must thus choose one vertex per pair with exactly one pair omitted. Such a transversal separates unselected same-side vertices using a selected counterpart of one index. For unselected opposite-side vertices a_i,b_j with i≠j, the only possible indistinguishability is S⊆{a_j,b_i}, which cannot occur when |S|=n-1>=3 (n>=4); in n=3 it occurs precisely for mixed-side transversals. Independent exhaustive code recomputed all subset signatures for sizes below n-1 and every n-1 subset for n=3..8, giving basis counts 6,32,80,192,448,1024 respectively; unrestricted n follows the argument, not this census.

originality.rationale: An especially relevant earlier published Resultary result (2026-10-04) classifies EDGE-metric crown bases by exactly one-hole transversals, n*2^(n-1) even at n=3. That is distinct from vertex adjacency metric dimension: its distances classify edges, while the present theorem distinguishes vertices with truncated d_2; the n=3 adjacency basis count is 6 versus 12 edge bases. For n>=4 the optimizers coincide, which creates substantial overlap, but the edge metric theorem alone does not logically furnish the adjacency vertex-separation condition and misses the 3-crown exception. The separate parameter, proof and exception are an original natural invariant best-of-knowledge; do not count the repeated large-n family as novel independent of the edge result.

value.rationale: Adjacency resolving sets and edge-metric resolving sets have different identification tasks. Their surprisingly coincident crown bases for n>=4 and sharply different n=3 boundary, alongside complete enumeration of all minimal vertex adjacency resolving sets, are precise natural graph-identification facts a future graph invariants researcher could need. Mathematical value rests on the independent vertex-classification and exceptional boundary, not on reprinting the known edge-metric basis count.

final_claim: For connected crown graph Cr_n=K_{n,n} minus a perfect matching, n>=3, adjacency dimension equals n-1. For n>=4 every one-hole matched-pair transversal is a basis (n*2^(n-1) in total); for n=3 only the six same-side two-vertex transversals are bases.
limitations: Different from edge metric dimension; published edge family overlaps for n>=4 and n=3 is exceptional.
No classification of larger resolving sets or k-adjacency bases.
